sam_acme: Hi @support, our March invoice (inv_20260301) doesn't match the dashboard. Dashboard shows £123.47 but the invoice PDF is £123.59. Can someone explain the 12p difference? I've attached screenshots and the PDF.

marie (Support): Thanks Sam — sorry about that. Can you paste the invoice id and account id here so I can escalate?

sam_acme: invoice id inv_20260301, account acme-123. No credits on the account. Dashboard shows total tokens 1,234,567 and unit cost 0.0001 => computed subtotal ~£102.88, VAT 20% -> £20.57, total ~£123.45. Invoice PDF shows subtotal £102.99, VAT £20.60, total £123.59. Screenshot uploaded.

marie (Support): @josh (Billing) tagging you — initial details above, customer seeing small mismatch between dashboard and billed PDF.

josh (Billing): On it. Sam, can you confirm currency on the account is GBP? Also confirm there were no manual adjustments. This often comes from per-line rounding or currency conversion. If you can attach the PDF that helps.

sam_acme: PDF uploaded. Currency is GBP, no manual adjustments. VAT applied at 20% on the invoice.

invoice-bot: [automated] invoice inv_20260301 generated at 2026-03-02T04:12:11Z. Currency=GBP. RoundingPolicy=PER_LINE(2). ExchangeRate=1.0000.

josh (Billing): Here's a small repro I ran that shows how per-line rounding can create differences vs aggregate dashboards. Example:
```
// simplified example
req1: 100000 tokens * 0.0001 = 10.0000 -> line -> £10.00
req2: 1234567 tokens * 0.0001 = 123.4567 -> line -> £123.46
sum_of_lines = £133.46
aggregate = (10.0000 + 123.4567) = 133.4567 -> round total = £133.46
// with many lines different individual roundings and VAT-per-line you can get off by a few pence
```

marie (Support): Also note VAT: our engine applies VAT per invoice line after rounding by currency (this is the tax/legal default for some regions). That can change the subtotal/VAT split compared to a dashboard that aggregates before VAT rounding.

lily (Finance): Confirming invoice engine currently uses per-line rounding for GBP invoices. That behavior is documented in our billing terms, but I agree we should show it more clearly in the UI.

sam_acme: Ok that explains the mechanism, but can you correct the billed amount? It screws with our bookkeeping to have unexplained deltas.

josh (Billing): Short-term: we can issue a one-time credit of £0.12 to reconcile the difference. Long-term: we will (1) add an "invoice rounding adjustment" line to show the delta on PDFs and (2) add a dashboard toggle to view values using the invoice rounding policy. Filing ENG ticket.

marie (Support): @sam_acme we've created a credit for £0.12 to account acme-123 and attached a note referencing inv_20260301. You should see the credit applied next billing cycle. :handshake:

invoice-bot: [automated] credit cr_20260303 created for account acme-123 amount=£0.12 reason="invoice rounding discrepancy".

sam_acme: Thanks, appreciate the quick turnaround. Please update docs so other customers aren't surprised.

josh (Billing): Will do — creating DOCS-482 for documentation update and ENG-857 to add the UI flag and explicit rounding adjustment line. Leaving this thread open until the credit posts.

marie (Support): Closing loop once credit is applied. If anything else pops up, ping this thread.

sam_acme: Received confirmation of the credit. All good, thanks everyone!
